facts.statement: Tenant Iven Rell reported a brown damp patch and overnight drips at the kitchen ceiling of 16 Brindlewick Mews on 10 June 2025; no sagging or fallen ceiling.
No light below the patch, kitchen sockets dry, no water near electrics at the time of report.
A young child is present in the flat and the tenant asked for a call on arrival; detail kept in the case record and not passed to the contractor.

Contractor Kellan Orve (Mossbarrow Pipe Services) inspected on 11 June and saw moisture at a compression joint above the ceiling hatch while the tap was running; the joint is not reachable through the hatch.

Estimate covers isolating the pipe, opening ~30 cm of ceiling lining, replacing the joint and making good; it excludes investigation, testing, removal and disposal of suspect material. No amount is stated in the case file.
Landlord Ossa Fenlow authorised the quoted plumbing scope up to the estimate amount on 12 June, subject to safe working and prior contact before any scope or cost increase.
Return visit was agreed with the tenant for 13 June 10:30-12:30; the contractor attended at 10:40 and was admitted.

A pale, fibrous-looking lining is visible behind the painted ceiling board; the contractor could not identify it, did not touch it, and paused the work. No drilling, cutting, sampling or removal has occurred at any visit; hatch left closed.
No survey, material assessment or ceiling alteration record exists: landlord has none, building manager has none and has not inspected the flat.
The leak is recurring: tenant reported a small drip on 13 June when the kitchen tap was used and has stopped using that tap; ceiling not visibly sagging.
Landlord confirmed on 13 June that her authorisation does not extend to a specialist material assessment and asked for likely cost and timing before considering further expenditure.
The contractor cannot price work involving the unidentified lining and cannot specify what assessment would be required.
No landlord standing spend cap is on file in this case record; default authority is therefore £0.

handover.question: Who sources and pays for an accredited asbestos survey of the kitchen ceiling lining at 16 Brindlewick Mews so the already-authorised pipe repair can proceed, and what cost and timing do we give the landlord?
summary: Plumber found moisture at a compression joint above the kitchen ceiling; unreachable through the hatch, so a ~30 cm ceiling opening was quoted (event-011).
Landlord Ossa Fenlow authorised the quoted plumbing scope only, subject to safe working, and must be asked before any scope or cost increase (event-013, event-022).

On the return visit the plumber saw a pale, fibrous-looking lining behind the ceiling board, could not identify it, paused and left; no drilling, cutting, sampling or removal occurred and the hatch is closed (event-017, event-018, event-023).
No survey or alteration record exists: landlord has none (event-013, event-022); building manager has none and has not inspected the flat (event-006).
Leak is live - tenant reported a drip when the kitchen tap was used on 13 June and has stopped using the tap; a young child lives in the flat; ceiling not sagging (event-020, event-007).
handover.gap: No accredited asbestos surveyor sourced or priced - the instructed plumber states he cannot specify or price the assessment (event-023) - and no landlord spend cap is on file (default £0), so the cost and timing the landlord asked for (event-022) cannot be given and nobody can be instructed.
options: Office sources an accredited asbestos surveyor, obtains a priced quote (sample and analysis) and puts it to the landlord for approval; repair resumes once the material is cleared or a licensed method is specified.
Ask the landlord to appoint her own surveyor (already offered in ACT-2): no agency spend, but timing leaves our control while the leak continues.

Wait for the landlord's reply to event-024 only: the leak recurs whenever the kitchen tap is used, the tenant is without normal use of the kitchen sink, and the s.11 reasonable-time clock from 10 June keeps running.
handover.recommended: Option 1: source and price an accredited asbestos survey now and put the quoted amount (with VAT and lead time) to the landlord; keep the plumbing instruction live but paused with Mossbarrow Pipe Services.
handover.default_if_timeout: If the landlord has not replied by 16 June (3-day wait from event-024, 13 June 15:26), the case returns to manual review as an expired landlord wait; the tenant stays on damage-limiting advice and the ceiling remains undisturbed.
handover.undo: Nothing irreversible: no surveyor instructed, no spend committed, no ceiling opened. The hold (ACT-4) can be lifted and the plumber re-booked for the already-approved scope once the lining is cleared.

uncertainty: The estimate amount for the plumbing scope is not stated anywhere in the case file, so no figure can be quoted to any party.

Whether the joint can be reached by any route that avoids the lining is unknown - the contractor says it cannot be reached through the hatch (event-011, event-023).
